stories.title: Radisson Blu Sheffield reaches net zero status
stories.summary: Radisson Blu Sheffield has received Verified Net Zero status, becoming the second Radisson property in the UK to achieve the recognition. The group aims to have 100 such hotels by 2030. Eleven properties in the portfolio currently hold the certification, which covers energy consumption under Scopes 1 and 2.

stories.title: India drops in global climate index
stories.summary: India has slipped five places to 28th in the Climate Change Performance Index 2027, retaining a medium rating. The report credits the country for expanding non-fossil electricity but notes a continued dependence on coal and the absence of a time-bound national energy transition roadmap.

stories.title: COP31 focuses on urban resilience finance
stories.summary: Over 100 national leaders and 600 CEOs met at COP31 to discuss investment in urban climate resilience. Organisers are prioritising early warning systems and infrastructure decarbonisation. COP31 President Murat Kurum stated that national climate commitments must now translate into tangible progress in cities where people live.

stories.title: Architecture faces climate reality at COP31
stories.summary: The climate crisis has become the primary design brief for the architecture industry. With buildings and construction accounting for a significant share of global emissions, the sector is being positioned as both a major contributor to the problem and a necessary component of the solution.

stories.title: Green Bengal Summit discusses sustainable growth
stories.summary: The CII Indian Green Building Council held the Green Bengal Summit 2026 in Kolkata to discuss climate-resilient development. The event brought together policymakers and architects to deliberate on future-proofing the state's built landscapes. The summit was anchored around the theme of regeneration and sustainable growth.

stories.title: Model law proposed for data center regulation
stories.summary: Climate Mayors has introduced a model local law to help cities manage data center development. The framework aims to provide guidance on siting, permitting, and community benefits, as officials note that data centers are currently moving at a scale that local codes were not built to handle.

stories.title: Meta secures low-carbon cement for data centers
stories.summary: Sublime Systems will supply low-carbon cement to Meta for future US data center construction. The agreement includes environmental attribute certificates tied to 180,000 tons of production. The manufacturer claims its technology eliminates kiln emissions and supports retrofits at existing facilities to reduce reliance on imported materials.

stories.title: Cement industry reports net zero progress
stories.summary: The Global Cement and Concrete Association presented a report at COP31 reviewing the sector's progress toward net zero. Industry leaders stated that cement remains essential for growing populations and requested enabling policies to bring transformative technologies to commercial scale. The industry is currently balancing emissions reductions with infrastructure demands.

stories.title: Algae-based building materials market grows
stories.summary: The global market for algae-based building materials is shifting from research to commercial viability. According to an IndexBox report, the sector is driven by carbon-negative construction mandates and more disciplined procurement. The market is projected to see broader adoption through 2035 as demand fundamentals continue to evolve.

stories.title: AD Design Show 2026 opens in Mumbai
stories.summary: The AD Design Show 2026 opened at the Jio World Convention Centre on November 13. The event featured a keynote address from industry figures and various activations. Partners for this year's edition include Quantra Surfaces, Racconti, Simpolo Tiles and Bathware, and Artize.

stories.title: Historic warehouse highlights maritime trade past
stories.summary: The centuries-old Pandagasalai Warehouse in Karaikal remains a rare example of a traditional river-port structure on the Coromandel Coast. Once a key logistical centre, the site illustrates a trading network where rivers served as commercial arteries before the development of modern roads and railways.

stories.title: Architects revisit traditional courtyard designs
stories.summary: Architects are increasingly incorporating courtyards into modern Indian homes to improve ventilation and natural connection. Once a defining feature of traditional architecture, these open-to-sky spaces are being adapted with internal gardens and contemporary layouts to bring the outdoors into residential design.

stories.title: Guwahati Airport expands with bamboo terminal
stories.summary: Guwahati Airport inaugurated a new integrated terminal built with over 140 tonnes of bamboo in December 2025. The hub serves as the primary connection point for Northeast India, handling 6.6 million passengers in the 2025 to 2026 financial year across its two terminals.

stories.title: West Bengal minister calls for green city expansion
stories.summary: Urban Development Minister Agnimitra Paul has called for green city blueprints to extend beyond Kolkata to urban centres including Durgapur and Siliguri. Speaking at the Green Bengal Summit, she stated that economic development and ecological responsibility must be integrated to address heatwaves and urban flooding.

stories.title: Green Bengal Summit advocates for net zero
stories.summary: The CII Indian Green Building Council hosted the Green Bengal Summit 2026 to discuss climate-resilient urbanisation. Officials emphasised that future-proofing is an essential economic prerequisite. The summit focused on strategies for sustainable development and the regeneration of built environments across the state.

stories.title: Danube sells out luxury Dubai penthouses
stories.summary: Danube Properties reported that all penthouses at its Shahrukhz Residences project in Dubai sold out on launch day. The waterfront units, designed by Gauri Khan, were priced at 50 crore rupees each. The project was unveiled at an event attended by Shah Rukh Khan and Gauri Khan.

stories.title: Built99 index ranks Indian architecture studios
stories.summary: The Built99 index has launched to highlight 99 Indian architecture studios based on finished projects. The list is backed by designboom and ArchDaily and aims to avoid pay-to-play rankings. Inclusion is by nomination only, requiring studios to demonstrate long-term cultural value and responsible construction practices.

stories.title: Chilean architect Smiljan Radic Clarke wins Pritzker Prize 2026
stories.summary: The Pritzker Prize jury described Smiljan Radic Clarke's work as optimistic and quietly joyful. The Chilean architect has completed more than 60 projects, including the Teatro del Biobio, which features a semi-translucent facade. The announcement of the winner was delayed in 2026. Architecture remains a patient profession.

stories.title: Zaha Hadid-designed London home hits market for £11.95 million
stories.summary: A private house at 6 Grosvenor Crescent Mews is for sale for £11.95 million. It is one of only two single-family homes completed by Zaha Hadid's studio during her lifetime. The property was constructed starting in 2014 and is now being offered for sale for the first time.

stories.title: Kengo Kuma reflects on six decades of architecture
stories.summary: Kengo Kuma decided to become an architect after seeing Kenzo Tange’s Yoyogi National Gymnasium as a ten-year-old. He has since built a varied body of work, including restaurants, residences, and public spaces. His buildings are noted for a quiet, low-profile character. The career path appears to have held.

stories.title: Adding insulation over existing drywall is discouraged
stories.summary: GreenBuildingAdvisor warns against adding insulation over existing drywall in brick houses. The practice can reduce the temperature of the plaster and potentially drop it below the dew point. The existing air gap between the brick and the drywall may also become a breeding ground for mold.

stories.title: Liu Jiakun holds first major solo exhibition in Shanghai
stories.summary: Pritzker Prize winner Liu Jiakun is hosting his first major solo exhibition at the Power Station of Art in Shanghai. The event follows recent market unease regarding the technology sector and ongoing scrutiny of growth prospects. The exhibition opened to the public on November 13, 2026.

stories.title: Kashef Chowdhury/URBANA wins inaugural MoMA prize
stories.summary: The Museum of Modern Art awarded its inaugural Ambasz to MoMA Annual Prize for Nature-Reconciled Architecture to the Friendship Centre in Bangladesh. The $200,000 prize recognizes projects that address the relationship between built and natural environments. Half of the funds are allocated to a non-profit organization for tree planting.

stories.title: Steven Holl designs colorful watch as tribute to Álvaro Siza
stories.summary: Watchmaker Cauny has released The Sculpture Watch, designed by Steven Holl. The piece draws on a dialogue between Holl and Álvaro Siza regarding color and architecture. Holl stated that watercolor painting, which is integral to his design process, served as the primary inspiration for the timepiece.

stories.title: Sustainable architecture in Brazil
stories.summary: The Canuanã school in Tocantins, Brazil, provides boarding facilities for 540 students from remote farming communities. Completed in 2017, the dormitories use locally sourced timber and earth bricks. A vast canopy shades the complex, and perforated walls are designed to allow air to pass through the structures.

stories.title: Mecanoo completes renovation of Netherlands Central Bank
stories.summary: Dutch firm Mecanoo has finished a major retrofit of De Nederlandsche Bank in Amsterdam. The project involved dismantling a 14-storey tower and opening up a former gold vault. The 1968 structure was previously described by some as the nation’s ugliest building. It is now a living room.

stories.title: Studio RAP installs ceramic facade on Dutch switchstation
stories.summary: Powerhouse Company commissioned Studio RAP to create a ceramic facade for a new electricity switchstation in Beverwijk. The artwork, titled Powerwall, visualizes electromagnetic fields as a relief on the building's exterior. The project aims to give essential energy infrastructure a public presence that invites curiosity from passersby.

stories.title: ETH Zurich researchers test bacteria-based building materials
stories.summary: Karen Antorveza Paez at ETH Zurich is researching whether microorganisms can act as collaborators in architecture. Her method combines sand, bacteria, and digital fabrication to produce solid building parts without heat-intensive kilns. The research explores the potential for living materials to be used in future construction projects.

stories.title: Transparent wood and solar PV combined for skylights
stories.summary: A research team at India’s Vellore Institute of Technology has designed a glazing system using transparent wood and transparent solar PV modules. The system is intended to generate electricity while maintaining transparency and blocking heat gain. The researchers conducted a thorough investigation into the performance of the materials.

stories.title: Magnesium slag shows potential for low-carbon concrete
stories.summary: A systematic review indicates that industrial magnesium slag can serve as a binder in cementitious materials. When processed via accelerated carbonation or mechanochemical activation, the slag can replace 20 to 30 percent of traditional binders. The study suggests this metallurgical residue can improve the strength of eco-friendly mortars.

stories.title: Axtra3D provides hardware for 3D printing services
stories.summary: Several 3D printing services, including Protolabs and Prinoa, are using the Axtra Workflow to produce high-quality parts. The system includes the Lumia X1 printer, software, and post-processing tools. These companies serve diverse markets ranging from dental devices to high-precision artery stents using the same underlying technology platform.

stories.title: 3D-printed RC ship uses spinning rotors for speed
stories.summary: A 5-foot, 3D-printed RC cargo ship equipped with four spinning Magnus effect rotors achieved a 20 percent increase in speed during timed runs. The rotors use spinning cylinders to manipulate airflow. Real-world shipping companies are currently testing similar rotor technology to reduce fuel consumption on large vessels.

stories.title: Modified 3D printer enables low-cost bioprinting research
stories.summary: Microbiologists at the University of Rochester converted a $450 Ender 3 printer into a bioprinter for engineered living materials. By adding a custom syringe pump, the team reduced hardware costs from $100,000 to under $500. The modification makes research into microbial macrostructures more accessible to academic laboratories.

stories.title: Icon 3D-prints commercial training center in San Antonio
stories.summary: Icon is using a large-scale printer to construct a 12,649-square-foot training and exhibition center for ASCO Equipment in San Antonio. The project features curved concrete walls and marks the company's largest commercial building to date. The facility will include an open training floor and an upstairs lounge.

stories.title: Energy Conservation Building Code remains unnotified
stories.summary: Nine months after the Chief Minister announced the Energy Conservation Building Code would be notified, the proposal remains with the PDD. The initiative was first moved in 2022 and has undergone four years of consultations. Despite public assurances, the code has yet to be officially implemented.

stories.title: Bengal summit discusses climate-resilient urban development
stories.summary: Policymakers, planners and developers gathered at the Green Bengal Summit in Kolkata to discuss greener buildings and water management. The event focused on future-proofing urban growth against rising temperatures and waterlogging. The city is currently examining ways to make its expanding urban spaces more resilient.

stories.title: Air purifiers and the role of AI in Indian cities
stories.summary: As air pollution levels rise, households are increasingly turning to technology to access clean air. The growing demand has highlighted the role of AI and connected infrastructure in managing air quality. Managing the air is becoming a routine task for many urban Indians.

stories.title: Urban flooding remains a persistent monsoon challenge
stories.summary: Urban flooding is rarely caused by heavy rainfall alone. In Indian cities, intense downpours interact with inadequate drainage, encroached floodplains and rapid urbanisation. Concrete surfaces prevent natural absorption, while poorly maintained waterways restrict movement. The water has nowhere else to go.

stories.title: Satellites hold untapped potential for development - www.daily-sun.com
IGBC summit focuses on future-proofing Bengal
stories.summary: The Confederation of Indian Industry’s Indian Green Building Council held its Green Bengal Summit in Kolkata to discuss climate-resilient development. The event brought together experts to examine integrated urban development and Net Zero carbon pathways. The theme for the gathering was future-proofing the region.

stories.title: West Bengal plans stricter wetland and rainwater rules
stories.summary: The state government is framing stricter norms for wetland conservation and making rainwater harvesting mandatory for new buildings. Urban development minister Agnimitra Paul cited New Town as a benchmark for green-city certification. The government intends to expand these green building incentives beyond Kolkata.

stories.title: Hisar administration transfers land for industrial smart city
stories.summary: The district administration has transferred 990 acres of land to the National Industrial Corridor Development Corporation for a new manufacturing cluster. The site is part of a national programme to develop 12 industrial smart cities. Hisar is the first of these sites to complete the transfer.

stories.title: Experts warn local governments are sidelined in planning
stories.summary: Speakers at a Dhaka dialogue argued that local government institutions are being sidelined in urban planning. Bureaucratic hurdles and political interference have reportedly reduced city corporations to waste management and mosquito control agencies. The trend is blamed for worsening infrastructure deficits and public suffering.

stories.title: Centralised planning blamed for urban infrastructure issues
stories.summary: Experts say local government institutions are being sidelined in urban development due to centralised decision-making. This shift has weakened city corporations, leaving them to focus primarily on waste management and mosquito control. The result is described as a decline in public participation and worsening civic conditions.

stories.title: Karachi opens sponge park to manage monsoon runoff
stories.summary: A new sponge park in Gulberg Town has been designed to hold up to 100,000 gallons of rainwater. The project aims to reduce surface run-off and urban flooding risks. Experts from WWF-Pakistan described the one-acre site as a practical example of turning climate commitments into actual experience.

stories.title: Architects advocate for sustainability in urban planning
stories.summary: A former sustainability director at Masdar City argues that the most consequential decisions about a building are made before construction begins. The approach integrates clean energy and thoughtful planning to ensure efficiency for decades. The energy transition requires a new, large-scale approach to how communities are designed.

stories.title: PeopleForBikes releases 2026 city rankings
stories.summary: The annual scores measure how well bike riders can connect to jobs, schools, healthcare and other destinations. The rankings evaluate the accessibility of urban infrastructure for cyclists across large US cities.

stories.title: Mayors call for federal housing funding , and guardrails to ensure it’s administered
stories.summary: Congress’ continuing resolution to fund the federal government expires Dec. 11.

stories.title: Report urges cities to plan for wildfire recovery
stories.summary: A new playbook suggests cities should establish partnerships with community development financial institutions to secure recovery funding. The report highlights the need to remove policy barriers that slow rebuilding efforts after wildfires. Financial planning is presented as a necessary component of urban resilience.

stories.title: Urban planning often overlooks children's needs
stories.summary: Indian cities are designed for adult convenience with limited consideration for children's safety or play. Exposure to pollutants has led to increased respiratory issues among adolescents. The lack of outdoor space is now cited as a factor in declining health outcomes for urban children.

stories.title: Serial founder raises pre-seed for AI that spots UK building projects before they start - Dealroom
CEPT University students develop AI safety tools
stories.summary: Students at CEPT University have created an AI-based system to monitor construction site safety. The project uses computer vision to detect helmets and protective vests from live camera feeds. The system is currently being tested at sites in Ahmedabad to automate safety checks.

stories.title: AI system automates construction site safety checks
stories.summary: A student project called SafeGuard uses computer vision and deep learning to monitor worker safety in real time. The system identifies whether employees are wearing helmets and vests from CCTV feeds. It aims to address the difficulties of manual safety supervision across large construction sites.

stories.title: Archeform BIM 1.1 aims to cut redraws for small SketchUp firms
stories.summary: Archeform BIM 1.1 is a 199 euro a year SketchUp extension that puts existing, demolished and new construction into a single model. The company says it aims to cut redraw time for small firms. Its success depends on whether the IFC export satisfies consultants and authorities.

stories.title: Exclusive | Zacua Ventures Raises $135 Million For Heavy-Industry Technology Bets - WSJ
Construction searches held up better than architecture in 2026
stories.summary: SignalHire data shows construction searches fell 19.94 percent in the first half of 2026, while architecture searches dropped 74.45 percent. The 54.51 point gap is the widest in the built environment group. The report notes these figures may not reflect broader industry activity.

stories.title: India sees rise in climate tech startups for 2027
stories.summary: Indian startups are targeting renewable energy, carbon removal and electric mobility as environmental challenges increase. The sector is emerging as a key area of innovation to address rising temperatures, unpredictable rainfall and waste generation. The demand for practical technology has grown considerably across the country.

stories.title: Shipping Corporation of India tenders 22 ships for 3.2 billion dollars
stories.summary: Shipping Corporation of India has called for bids to construct 22 ships, including gas carriers and container vessels, at a cost of 3.2 billion dollars. The move supports a government plan to make India one of the top five shipbuilders globally by 2047.

stories.title: MooyoungCM | Digital construction management - Autodesk
Researchers turn moon dust into LEGO-like bricks
stories.summary: University of Arkansas researchers have demonstrated that simulated lunar dust can be 3D printed into interlocking bricks without adding other materials. The approach aims to reduce the construction supplies NASA would need to transport to the Moon. Future lunar bases may resemble giant assembly projects.

stories.title: CEPT University to accept UCEED and NID DAT 2027 scores
stories.summary: CEPT University will accept UCEED 2027 and NID DAT 2027 scores for its BDes Hons programme. Applicants with these scores are exempt from the university's separate entrance test for the 2027 cycle. The change provides students with two national level examination options for admission.

stories.title: Tyler School of Art and Architecture graduation set for May 7
stories.summary: The Tyler School of Art and Architecture graduation ceremony will take place on May 7 at 2:30 p.m. in McGonigle Hall. A reception in the Tyler building will precede the event. The ceremony is open to faculty, staff, parents and students.

stories.title: Elizabeth Diller preserves memory in MIT architecture project
stories.summary: Elizabeth Diller designed the new MIT School of Architecture and Planning space by exposing the structure of the former Metropolitan Storage Warehouse. She argues that covering or painting over old buildings removes the history of cities. The design aims to keep the building's memories alive.

stories.title: Sapp Design Architects helps tornado-ravaged high school - Springfield Business Journal
Cedar Rapids schools announce new career academies
stories.summary: The Cedar Rapids Community School District will launch career academies at three high schools for the 2027-28 academic year. Students can earn college credit and gain experience in fields including health care, engineering and creative media. The programs aim to improve college and career readiness.

stories.title: CEPT University updates BDes Hons admission criteria
stories.summary: CEPT University will accept UCEED 2027 and NID DAT 2027 scores for its five-year Bachelor of Design programme. Applicants with valid scores from these national exams are exempt from the university entrance test. Applications for the 2027 session remain open until November 30.

stories.title: Students propose architecture projects for public spaces
stories.summary: The Abitare il Paese project involved 2,247 students in proposals to improve local parks and streets. Ideas included solar-powered benches and turning parks into open-air cinemas. The initiative aims to train students to be attentive to the care of the places they inhabit.

research.title: Physicists use laser light to unlock a crystal's hidden electrical powers
research.summary: Scientists have discovered how to use flashes of laser light to organize tiny electrical regions inside a crystal, solving a decades-old mystery about how the material behaves. The laser-induced alignment lasts just a trillionth of a second, but the breakthrough could open the door to new ways of.
